localBiteReport: The week of September 4–10, 2026 brought the first signs of the fall transition to Choctawhatchee Bay, with water beginning to cool slightly and large concentrations of baitfish pushing into bayous, flats, bridge areas, and roll-downs across the bay. Capt. Blake Nelson (Last Cast Charters) reported that redfish and general flats activity are expected to improve steadily over the coming weeks as the seasonal shift continues, with slot reds and bull reds both in the picture. Bait schools — primarily greenies — are now accessible in shallower inshore structure, setting up better opportunities for redfish on the flats as September progresses. Water temperature at this location measured 87°F. These details are from a report dated September 4–10, 2026, roughly one week old at time of writing.
